official_references.title: How to Manually Repair a VMware Replica created by Veeam (KB1773)
official_references.scope: Veeam Backup & Replication 12-13.1 VMware replica repair; not applicable to CDP or Cloud Connect replicas

entries.compatibility_scope: Existing replica signatures; operation-specific VMware gates retained.
entries.limitations: Reference knowledge is not proof of root cause. Existing replica signatures; operation-specific VMware gates retained.

diagnostic_guidance.evidence_basis: Veeam KB1773 (applies to VBR 12, 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 12.3.1, 12.3.2, 13, 13.1), page text read 2026-11-20 through a model-extracted fetch; human re-read pending. EIMS signatures RevertSnapshot/InvalidSnapshotFormat are not named in the article, so the mapping from this EIMS signal to the article is an inference.
expected_findings: Vendor-listed replica failure messages: "Invalid Snapshot Configuration", "Unable to repair replica VM", "File or folder already exists" when creating a snapshot on the replica, and "CID mismatch error: The parent virtual disk has been modified since the child was created".
Applies to VMware replicas created by Veeam only; the article states it is not applicable to CDP replicas or Cloud Connect replicas.
safe_remediation: Stop other replication jobs that target the same replica destination and check target proxies for stuck hot-added replica disks before changing the replica (vendor step; hot-add cleanup is in Veeam KB1775).
Optionally clone the replica in VMware first; if the clone works, map the replication job to the clone (vendor step).

Repair is performed on the REPLICA VM only and is described by the vendor as intentionally destructive to replica data; follow the full KB1773 procedure and, if it does not resolve the failure, open a Veeam Support case (vendor guidance).
diagnostic_guidance.risk: Vendor states the procedure must never be performed on a production VM because it intentionally causes data loss; acceptable only for a Veeam replica, which is repaired on the next replication run.
diagnostic_guidance.rollback: The vendor article provides no rollback. Before editing, record which disk files map to each SCSI ID and the VM configuration file location (vendor step); the replica itself is rebuilt by the next replication job run.
verification_criteria: Creating and then removing a snapshot on the replica completes without error (vendor test step), then the replica is re-added to the job, remapped and the replication job runs successfully.

expected_findings: ACL compilation ran out of memory; the previously compiled lists stay in use and changes since the last successful compilation are removed.

verification_criteria: A later ACL compilation completes without message 106024 (inference; the source page does not state a check).
